CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-COMMS-ONLY-SUFFICIENT.statement: The core problem is inadequate customer communication about charges; drafting apology replies addresses the need, and no payment-system fix is required.

H-GATEWAY-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED.statement: A payment gateway configuration change disabled or weakened idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries, causing retried captures to be charged twice.

H-SHOP-RETRY-NO-IDEMPOTENCY.statement: The checkout-to-payment process (P-PAY) resends capture requests over handoff H-CAPTURE without attaching idempotency keys, independent of gateway configuration.

H-PSP-SIDE-DUPLICATE-PROCESSIN.statement: The payment service provider (ORG-PSP) processes a capture twice even when a correct idempotency key is supplied, i.e., a vendor-side defect.

H-LEDGER-DOUBLE-COUNT-ARTIFACT.statement: Customers were not actually charged twice by the PSP; DA-CHG double-records a single successful capture, making the complaints a reporting/reconciliation artifact.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The config-audit log shows SH-PAY turned idempotency_key_enforcement from on to off on 2026-09-09 (CHG-77) for temporary latency debugging, and the rollback was never executed, so the gateway is still running with enforcement disabled.

The authoritative payments-db daily breakdown shows orders_with_2_captures stayed at 0 on 09-07 and 09-08 despite ~117-121 gateway timeout retries, then jumped to counts nearly matching the retry totals (118 and 124) on 09-09 and 09-10, the same date CHG-77 disabled idempotency enforcement. This tightly links real double-captures to the config change interacting with timeout retries, not to communication, ledger artifacts, PSP-side defects, or missing idempotency keys in the checkout flow.

PSP-side logs (independent of payments-db) show that during 2026-09-01..08 all 238 gateway timeout retries carried idempotency keys and were deduplicated by PSP (0 duplicate orders), whereas during 2026-09-09..10 (after CHG-77) all 242 duplicate orders came from gateway timeout retries sent with no idempotency key, with zero duplicates from any other path. This pinpoints the mechanism: disabling idempotency enforcement stopped idempotency keys from accompanying capture retries, so PSP could no longer deduplicate them, producing real double charges.

crm-tickets weekly counts show double-charge complaints stayed near-flat (9, 11) in weeks W35-W36 then jumped sharply to 288 and 301 in W37-W38 while order volume stayed roughly constant (~21k/week), i.e. a ~25x increase in complaint rate that begins in the week containing 2026-09-09, the date CHG-77 disabled gateway idempotency enforcement per E-01. This independently corroborates, from the customer-facing side, that the real driver of the surge in double-charge complaints is the technical config change already pinned down by E-02/E-03, not a pre-existing or steady-state issue.

E-05.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-PAY, the engineer who executed CHG-77, confirms in interview that idempotency-key enforcement on the gateway was switched off on 09-09 for temporary latency debugging and never rolled back, and explains the mechanism: gateway timeout retries have always occurred at a steady rate, but without the idempotency key the PSP no longer dedupes the retried capture, producing a real double charge. He also states re-enabling is a single-setting change via the gateway config tool but requires payments-operations runtime confirmation.

E-06.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-CS (the original requester) reiterates the initial framing: the issue is customer anger over double charges and the fix needed is faster/nicer apology replies. This is an unverified restatement of CL-01's framing and does not engage with the gateway-config root cause already pinned down by E-01-E-05.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The payments change runbook §4 (authoritative document) confirms that automation may execute set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config only with runtime confirmation from the payments operations manager (SH-OPS), and states the change is reversible. This corroborates the existing authorization constraint K-GW rather than revealing anything new about the root cause.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice.
symptoms: Double-charge support tickets jumped from 9-11/week (W35-W36) to 288-301/week (W37-W38) while order volume stayed flat (~20500-21400/week) (E-04).
orders_with_2_captures jumped from 0 (09-07, 09-08) to counts nearly matching that day's gateway timeout retries (118, 124) on 09-09/09-10 despite similar retry volumes on prior days (E-02).
problem_definition.root_problem: Since CHG-77 on 2026-09-09, idempotency-key enforcement on the payment gateway has been disabled, so the gateway's steady-rate timeout capture retries are sent to the PSP without idempotency keys and the PSP can no longer dedupe them, producing real double captures matching retry volumes and driving a ~25x surge in double-charge support tickets starting that week (E-01,E-02,E-03,E-04,E-05).

proposal.summary: The customer-service team (SH-CS) originally asked for an AI assistant to draft apology replies to customers complaining about double charges (CL-01, CL-03). Investigation of the gateway config audit, payments ledger, PSP logs, and support tickets instead traced the real root cause to a payment-gateway change: on 2026-09-09 payments engineer SH-PAY disabled idempotency-key enforcement via CHG-77 for latency debugging and never rolled it back (F-01/E-01, corroborated by SH-PAY interview E-05). From that date, steady-rate gateway timeout retries stopped carrying idempotency keys, so the PSP could no longer dedupe them, producing real double captures that closely track retry volumes (F-02/E-02, F-03/E-03) and a roughly 25x surge in double-charge support tickets (F-04/E-04). The hypothesis that this was merely a communication problem (H-COMMS-ONLY-SUFFICIENT) was rejected as contradicted by E-01-E-05 and E-08; the gateway-config root cause (H-GATEWAY-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED) was confirmed. The released work re-enables idempotency-key enforcement on the gateway (set_capture_idempotency, with required SH-OPS runtime confirmation per K-GW/E-07), verifies the fix against the payments-db duplicate-capture metric, and (where runtime allows) monitors ticket volume for a return to baseline. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, not a hold: the core fix is reversible, authorized, and its effect has started to be checked, but several verification items remain open and are documented as explicit limitations rather than blockers.
key_points: Root cause confirmed: CHG-77 disabled gateway idempotency-key enforcement on 2026-09-09, causing timeout retries to reach the PSP without keys and be double-captured, matching retry volumes day-for-day (F-01/E-01, F-02/E-02, F-03/E-03, F-04/E-04).

The requester's framing that this was a communication gap needing apology replies (CL-01, CL-03, E-06) was tested and rejected (H-COMMS-ONLY-SUFFICIENT, contradicted by E-01, E-02, E-03, E-04, E-05, E-08).

Released scope: re-enable idempotency enforcement on gateway-config (set_capture_idempotency, with mandatory SH-OPS runtime confirmation per constraint K-GW and runbook E-07), verify the fix via payments-db, and monitor crm-tickets ticket volume.

A concrete financial-harm finding was identified: 4 currently unrefunded double-captured orders totaling $227.40 (O-90211, O-90244, O-90302, O-90318) per F-06/E-08; the related unknown U-AFFECTED-ORDERS-REMEDIATION was resolved via VOB-U-AFFECTED-ORDERS-REMEDIATION.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no hold items) because the fix is reversible, authorized, and partially verified, while remaining open questions are tracked as explicit limitations/VOBs rather than release blockers.
